In triangle $ABC$, $A = 40°$, $B = 75°$, and $a = 8$ cm. Find side $b$.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{a}{\sin A} &= \frac{b}{\sin B} \\ \frac{8}{\sin 40°} &= \frac{b}{\sin 75°} \\ \frac{8}{0.6428} &= \frac{b}{0.9659} \\ b &= \frac{8 \times 0.9659}{0.6428} \\ b &= 12.0 \text{ cm (1 d.p.)} \end{aligned}$$
In triangle $PQR$, $P = 55°$, $R = 48°$, and $p = 10$ cm. Find side $r$.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{p}{\sin P} &= \frac{r}{\sin R} \\ \frac{10}{\sin 55°} &= \frac{r}{\sin 48°} \\ r &= \frac{10 \times \sin 48°}{\sin 55°} \\ r &= \frac{10 \times 0.7431}{0.8192} \\ r &= 9.1 \text{ cm (1 d.p.)} \end{aligned}$$
In triangle $ABC$, $a = 12$ cm, $b = 9$ cm, and $A = 65°$. Find angle $B$.

$$\begin{aligned} \frac{\sin A}{a} &= \frac{\sin B}{b} \\ \frac{\sin 65°}{12} &= \frac{\sin B}{9} \\ \sin B &= \frac{9 \times \sin 65°}{12} \\ \sin B &= \frac{9 \times 0.9063}{12} \\ \sin B &= 0.6797 \\ B &= \sin^{-1}(0.6797) \\ B &= 42.8° \text{ (1 d.p.)} \end{aligned}$$

A surveyor measures the following: from point A, the angle to a tree at C is 40°. From point B (50 m from A), the angle to C is 65°. Points A and B are in a straight line with the angle $ABC = 65°$. Find the distance $AC$. (1 d.p.)
Show that in any triangle, $\frac{a}{b} = \frac{\sin A}{\sin B}$.
In triangle $ABC$, prove that the area can be written as $\frac{a^2 \sin B \sin C}{2 \sin A}$.

Area $= \frac{1}{2}ab\sin C$. By the sine rule, $b = \frac{a\sin B}{\sin A}$. Substituting: Area $= \frac{1}{2}a \cdot \frac{a\sin B}{\sin A} \cdot \sin C = \frac{a^2 \sin B \sin C}{2\sin A}$. ✓
